messages:
raj: quick perf snapshot from this morning comparing live (SSE/ws) streaming vs request-response (non-streaming) across GPUs/regions. saw an odd inversion — streaming gives better p50 but worse p95 on H100 in eu-west-1. link to dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/runs/1823

michelle: can you paste the key numbers?

raj: sure. trimmed to essentials:
```
Config: model=vicuna-13b-qa, quant=q4_0, seq=1024
us-west-2 (A100):
  non-stream p50=78ms, p95=210ms, throughput(1c)=42 tok/s
  streaming   p50=65ms, p95=260ms, throughput(1c)=47 tok/s
eu-west-1 (H100):
  non-stream p50=72ms, p95=220ms, throughput(1c)=50 tok/s
  streaming   p50=60ms, p95=340ms, throughput(1c)=58 tok/s
Notes: batch=1 run, kernel_hint=auto, kv_cache=off
```

sasha: thanks. pattern looks like streaming improves avg latency & sustained throughput but amplifies tail on H100 eu-west. could be backpressure / event-loop queueing on websocket worker threads. did you run with continuous batching enabled?

raj: yes continuous batching was on for both modes. queue depth looked spiky on the H100 hosts.

michelle: two immediate hypotheses: (1) kernel selection on H100 switched to 'cutlass_fused' for certain sequence lengths causing occasional slow paths, (2) region-level network jitter -> SSE/WS keeps a connection open so tail exposed. non-stream opens more connections but each is shorter.

ben: can we rule out GC / python worker hiccups? which runtime?

raj: runtime is native-serving v2.4 (C++ runtime), per-process memory stable. no python GC.

ci-bot: automated run 1823456789-ci: all checks passed, per-host logs uploaded: https://ci.redwood.ai/logs/1823456789

michelle: ok next steps: collect per-request trace for the p95 on H100 eu-west-1, and re-run streaming with kernel_hint=triton_fast and kernel_hint=cutlass_base to see kernel sensitivity. also flip kv_cache=on for streamed sessions (should reduce duplicate prefix compute).

raj: will do. added a quick wrk scenario for repeatability:
```
# non-streaming HTTP test
wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --latency http://ingress.us-west-2.redwood/v1/generate
# streaming test (sse runner)
./tools/sse-bench --clients 200 --duration 60 --url ws://ingress.eu-west-1.redwood/v1/stream
```

sasha: when you post traces include kernel selection logs from /var/log/redwood/runtime-kernels.log and the serving header `x-redwood-kernel` in response. that header tells which codepath handled the request.

raj: logging those. one more oddity: H100 hosts show higher throughput but also more variance in token-per-second when streaming. suggests periodic slow kernels or networking stalls.

michelle: agree. also try lowering keepalive interval on the loadgen (50ms -> 200ms) to see if more aggressive pinging helps windowing/backpressure.

ben: if tail persists, we should test tombstoning fallback (route streaming to dedicated low-latency pool) to see if it's infra vs model runtime. can we repro on a cold host in us-east-1?

raj: spinning a cold H100 in us-east-1 now, will run both kernel hints + kv_cache + keepalive tuning. posting raw csv and short summary when done. thanks :thumbsup:

michelle: great. assign follow-ups: raj (re-run & traces), sasha (analyze kernel logs), ben (capacity fallback test). ping me when results are in. :eyes:
